title: Non-bearer auth schemes: HTTP Basic
description: HTTP Basic, the one bounded extension spec 9.2 still defers after Bearer (reading recorded on WCLI-9). Spec 9.2: Add HTTP Basic only if it passes the same safety tests; it is a bounded extension, not a reason to delay the first valid consumption flow. The custom API-key header case is delivered by WCLI-84 under DEC-248 (opum-ai/opum-doc#1490; docs/adr/0024), which narrowed this task to Basic. Basic may not land without the same approval-binding (T13-class) and credential non-disclosure (T14-class) evidence bearer and the header scheme carry; the audit half additionally needs WCLI-11.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A custom API-key header scheme passes the same safety tests as bearer: a changed header name, auth alias or binding cannot reuse an approval (T13-class), and the credential reaches only the approved header and is absent from argv, environment, files, output and audit (T14-class)
HTTP Basic passes the same safety tests, with the username source and exact byte shape recorded in the approved snapshot and never interpolated into a URL or a non-auth header
An unsupported or unknown auth type is rejected at approval time without echoing the submitted type or value, and a change of auth type invalidates any prior approval

implementationNotes: Narrowed to HTTP Basic by DEC-248 (opum-ai/opum-doc#1490), 2026-10-29. Acceptance criterion 1 (custom API-key header) is the scheme WCLI-84 delivers; it is left as written and unticked here, to be dispositioned when WCLI-84 closes.
